newsitem.title: UK: P&O shares gain after top-end profits.
newsitem.headline: P&O shares gain after top-end profits.

text.p: Shares in Peninsular & Oriental Steam Navigation Co Plc rose in pre-market trading on Tuesday after annual profits at the top end of analysts' expectations.
"The figures look quite strong and the shares should go up on the back of them," said one senior trader.
The stock was up 11p at 636-1/2 by 0804 GMT, extending a rebound since it dropped to a two-month low of 615p last Friday.
Pre-tax profit rose six percent to 332.8 million stg in 1996 compared with analyst expectations in a range between 251.6 million stg and 334 million. The dividend was unchanged at 30.5p, as expected.
The company repeated Monday's rejection of press reports that it was facing delays to its disposal plans, saying the programme was ahead of schedule.

Chairman Lord Sterling said: "Underlying profitability is set to improve sharply although restructuring in containers and ferries will constrain the 1997 results. The full impact of the measures we are taking will start to come through strongly in 1998."
